big_case.notes: Paid certiorari petition from the Georgia Court of Appeals presenting a recurring post-Mallory Fourteenth Amendment question—whether corporate registration under a statute lacking express jurisdictional notice (Georgia's Cooper Tire regime) constitutes valid consent to general personal jurisdiction, especially where registration predated the judicial construction. While the abstract doctrinal issue carries meaningful commercial salience across roughly three dozen states and drew an Atlantic Legal Foundation amicus brief plus a Call for a Response, this specific case arose from a procedurally encumbered $10.86M Chatham County default judgment with severe state-law preservation and deemed-admission complications, and ended in a routine summary denial on the first conference after briefing with no noted dissents.
